newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian consumers will fuel economic recovery, bank says.
newsitem.headline: Canadian consumers will fuel economic recovery, bank says.

text.p: Canadian consumers are preparing to open up their wallets and begin fueling an economic boom, despite data indicating otherwise, said an economist with one of Canada's largest banks on Sunday.

"Consumers are ready, willing and able," Rick Egelton, deputy chief economist with the Bank of Montreal said in a press release. "Over the next 18 months, as the recovery takes hold and employment gains continue, we expect consumer spending to increase three-and-a-half percent.''

Egelton dismissed the notion that a reported decline in the personal savings rate combined with the rapid rise in household debt meant the Canadian consumer would not play a significant role in the emerging economic expansion.

When the declining cost of servicing debt and the sharp rise in the value of consumers' financial and non-financial assets were taken into consideration, Canadian consumers had a healthy financial outlook, Egelton said.
The net worth of the Canadian consumer has risen substantially during the 1990s, Egelton added.
Broad-based improvements in the Canadian economy would also boost rising consumer confidence, Egelton said.
"Employment has finally started to show sustained gains. The expected increases in personal income will, in turn, facilitate healthy growth in consumer spending,'' Egelton predicted.
